subject: math.LO
name: Soundness theorem for first-order logic
statement: For classical first-order logic with its standard natural-deduction rules, if a sentence φ is formally derivable from a set Γ of sentences, then every structure satisfying Γ also satisfies φ. In symbols, Γ ⊢ φ implies Γ ⊨ φ.

subject: math.LO
name: Gödel completeness theorem
statement: For classical first-order logic, if every structure satisfying a set Γ of sentences also satisfies a sentence φ, then φ has a formal proof from Γ. Equivalently, every syntactically consistent first-order theory has a model.

subject: math.LO
name: Compactness theorem
statement: A set of first-order sentences has a model if and only if each of its finite subsets has a model. The theorem applies to arbitrary first-order languages and arbitrary sets of sentences.

subject: math.LO
name: Downward Löwenheim–Skolem theorem
statement: If M is a structure in a first-order language L and A is a subset of its domain, then M has an elementary substructure containing A with cardinality at most max(|A|, |L|, ℵ₀). In particular, a theory in a countable language that has an infinite model has a countably infinite model.

subject: math.LO
name: Upward Löwenheim–Skolem theorem
statement: If a first-order theory in a language L has an infinite model, then it has a model of every infinite cardinality κ ≥ |L|. Consequently, first-order theories with infinite models cannot specify a unique infinite cardinality for their models.

subject: math.LO
name: Gödel–Rosser first incompleteness theorem
statement: Every consistent, computably enumerable first-order theory in the language of arithmetic that extends Robinson arithmetic Q is incomplete. There is an arithmetic sentence φ for which neither φ nor its negation is provable in the theory.

subject: math.LO
name: Gödel second incompleteness theorem
statement: Let T be a consistent, computably enumerable theory extending first-order Peano arithmetic. For the usual arithmetized provability predicate for T, the theory T cannot prove its own consistency statement Con(T), which asserts that no T-proof of a contradiction exists.

subject: math.LO
name: Church’s undecidability theorem
statement: There is no algorithm that, given an arbitrary first-order sentence, always halts and decides whether that sentence is true in every structure. Thus the validity problem for unrestricted classical first-order logic is undecidable.

subject: math.LO
name: Undecidability of the halting problem
statement: There is no algorithm that, given a description of an arbitrary Turing machine and an input, always halts and correctly decides whether that machine halts on that input. This holds even though halting computations can be detected by simulation when they occur.

subject: math.LO
name: Tarski undefinability theorem
statement: The set of Gödel numbers of first-order arithmetic sentences true in the standard natural numbers is not definable by any first-order formula in the language of arithmetic. In particular, arithmetic has no internal formula that correctly expresses truth for all of its own sentences.

subject: math.LO
name: Craig interpolation theorem
statement: If first-order sentences φ and ψ satisfy φ ⊨ ψ, then there is a first-order sentence θ such that φ ⊨ θ and θ ⊨ ψ. Every nonlogical symbol occurring in θ occurs in both φ and ψ.

subject: math.LO
name: Beth definability theorem
statement: Let T be a first-order theory in a language L expanded by a relation symbol R. If any two models of T with the same L-reduct interpret R identically, then an L-formula φ exists such that T entails ∀x̄ (R(x̄) ↔ φ(x̄)).

subject: math.LO
name: Robinson joint consistency theorem
statement: Let L₁ and L₂ be first-order languages with intersection L₀, and let T₀ be a complete consistent L₀-theory. If T₁ and T₂ are consistent theories in L₁ and L₂ respectively, both containing T₀, then T₁ ∪ T₂ is consistent.

subject: math.LO
name: Gentzen cut-elimination theorem
statement: Every sequent derivable in Gentzen’s classical first-order sequent calculus LK has a derivation containing no applications of the cut rule. The corresponding result also holds for his intuitionistic calculus LJ.

subject: math.LO
name: Herbrand theorem
statement: Let ∃x̄ φ(x̄) be an existential sentence of first-order logic without equality, with φ quantifier-free and with at least one constant symbol available in the language. This sentence is valid if and only if some finite disjunction φ(t̄₁) ∨ ⋯ ∨ φ(t̄ₘ) of ground-term instances is a propositional tautology, treating ground atomic formulas as propositional variables.

subject: math.LO
name: Rice’s theorem
statement: Every nontrivial property of the partial functions computed by Turing machines is undecidable from a machine’s description. Here the property must depend only on the computed partial function, and nontrivial means that some partial computable functions have the property and some do not.

subject: math.LO
name: Post’s theorem
statement: For every integer n ≥ 1, a subset of the natural numbers belongs to the arithmetical class Σ⁰ₙ exactly when it is computably enumerable relative to the (n − 1)-st Turing jump of the empty set. It belongs to Δ⁰ₙ exactly when it is computable relative to that same oracle, with the zeroth jump equal to the empty set.

subject: math.LO
name: Cantor’s theorem
statement: For every set A, there is no surjective function from A onto its power set P(A). Since a ↦ {a} is an injection from A into P(A), the power set has strictly greater cardinality than A.

subject: math.LO
name: Gödel’s constructible-universe theorem
statement: Within ZF set theory, the class L of constructible sets is an inner model satisfying ZFC and the generalized continuum hypothesis. Consequently, if ZF is consistent, then ZFC together with the generalized continuum hypothesis is consistent.

subject: math.LO
name: Cohen’s independence theorem for the continuum hypothesis
statement: If ZFC is consistent, then both ZFC plus the continuum hypothesis and ZFC plus its negation are consistent. Hence, assuming ZFC is consistent, neither the continuum hypothesis nor its negation can be proved from ZFC; the relative consistency of its negation is obtained by forcing.
